newsitem.title: USA: Administaff boosts IPO price range to $15-$17.
newsitem.headline: Administaff boosts IPO price range to $15-$17.

text.p: Administaff Inc has raised the estimated price range for shares in its initial public offering to $15 to $17, signalling strong demand for the deal.
The price range for shares is now $15 to $17 each, lead underwriter Morgan Stanley said, up from its prior estimate of $13 to $15.
IPO analysts have said the deal is a hot one and could reap premiums of a point or more at its market debut.

Administaff provides adminstrative services like payroll, benefits, and human resources to small businesses. About 80 percent of its revenues are generated in its home state of Texas. It posted net income of $1.1 million on 1995 revenues of $716 million, according to its prospectus.
The deal is expected to price tonight for trading tomorrow on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol, Morgan Stanley said.

Underwriters and companies agree on a pricing range for the new shares based on their estimate of fair valuation for the company and preliminary indications of demand, and file it with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, usually a few weeks before IPO. If a deal prices below the range, it is a sign of weak demand for the deal, and vice versa.
